manoscritti.datazione: Possibly 13th century CE. Note: As the final folios with the colophon are missing, the manuscript is undated, but it looks very old. Although exact parallels are hard to find, its script resembles that of a manuscript of the Mohacūḍottara kept in the National Archives of Kathmandu, Nepal (Acc. NAK 4/1622 = NGMCP B 27/18), dated 806, which according to Diwakar Acharya is a date of the Valabhi era, therefore corresponding to 1125 CE (see Tāntrikābhidhānakośa II , p. 174, s.v. gaṇa ). This suggests a western or central Indian origin also for the Cambridge manuscript. It is worth noting that Yaśodhara, the author of the Jayamaṅgala , is generally assigned to the 13th century. If the latter date is reliable, Add.2251.1 would be an early copy of Yaśodhara’s work prepared not long after its composition, possibly from a source in a different script that the scribe did not know well, since complex ligatures (i.e. consonant clusters) are often erroneously reproduced.
